title: Four lepers (2 Kings 7:3–9)
hookLine: outcasts find the enemy camp empty and decide to share the news

lines: WHY SIT WE HERE UNTIL WE DIE?
cards: Outside the gate of Samaria sit four men with a skin disease. The law keeps them outside the city, and the city is under siege by Aram, with famine inside. They do the math out loud: "Why sit we here until we die?"
If we go into the city, there's famine, and we die there. If we sit here, we die here. So let's go over to the enemy camp.
If they spare us, we live. If they kill us, we were dying anyway. At twilight, the four outcasts get up and walk toward the enemy.

teach.h: WHY SIT WE HERE UNTIL WE DIE?
teach.b: They reach the edge of the camp, and there's no one there.
The Lord had made the army of Aram hear a noise of chariots and horses, the noise of a great host, and they fled in the twilight, leaving their tents, horses, donkeys, everything.

teach.h: AN EMPTY CAMP FULL OF FOOD.
teach.b: So four hungry men walk into an empty camp full of food. They eat and drink in one tent, carry off silver, gold and clothing, and hide it. Then another tent.
Who could blame them? And then they stop.

One says: "We do not well: this day is a day of good tidings, and we hold our peace." These are the men the law kept outside the walls, and they're the ones who realize good news kept to yourself goes bad.
They admit a plain worry, too: if we wait until morning light, some trouble will come upon us.
So they go back in the dark and call to the gatekeepers: we came to the camp of Aram, and no one was there, only horses tied, and donkeys tied, and the tents as they were. The king suspects a trap.
Scouts go out, find a trail of clothes and gear all the way to the Jordan. And the starving city walks out and eats.
The good news came from the edge, from four people nobody expected to hear from. It reached the city because they decided a full stomach wasn't enough. A day of good tidings has to be told.

how: Jews read the story of the four lepers as a haftarah alongside the Torah's laws for healing from skin disease in Leviticus.

o: four outcasts who found an empty camp and told it
four scouts the king sent out to the Jordan
four soldiers who guarded the gate of Samaria

games.q: you're one of four outcasts. you find the enemy camp empty and full of food, while the city starves. what do you do?
o: eat, hide what you can, and say nothing.
go back in the dark and tell the city.
games.why: they begin by hiding treasure, then stop: we do not well. this day is a day of good tidings. they tell the gatekeepers that night.

practice: Ask yourself what good thing you know that someone else doesn't: a job opening a friend could use, a thank-you you never passed on, praise you've said behind someone's back but never to their face.
Let one come to mind, along with the person who needs it, and hold it ready, like the four men at the gate in the dark.

wordCard.voice: Four lepers. Outcasts at the gate of a starving city who found the enemy camp empty and decided they couldn't keep the news to themselves. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a day of good tidings, from the four men's words in 2 Kings 7:9.

carryVoice: Your line: a day of good tidings. The news came from outside the walls. That's day seven hundred seventy-six.
